content.title: About
content.content: Corn chips, plain (Fritos) are crunchy corn snacks without added flavors or spices. They are made from whole‑grain corn flour, water, vegetable oil and salt, then fried until golden. The product is popular as a stand‑alone snack and as a base for Mexican‑style dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Fritos were first introduced in 1932 by The Frito Company in Texas.
Corn chips are made from whole‑grain corn flour, giving them a denser texture than potato chips.
The original recipe contains no artificial colors or flavorings.
Fritos are commonly used as a base for nachos and taco salads.
In the United States, plain corn chips rank among the top‑selling snack items in the no‑flavor category.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Corn chips provide complex carbs that supply sustained energy and help keep you feeling full.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain corn contributes a modest amount of fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Corn contains non‑heme iron, which contributes to hemoglobin formation.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: Unlike many sweet snacks, these chips contain virtually no sugar.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Corn supplies thiamine (B1) and niacin (B3), which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: The salt used in production can contribute to elevated blood pressure if consumed in excess.

items.title: Calorie density
items.content: Chips are energy‑dense; portion control is recommended to avoid over‑consumption.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may be allergic to corn products.

items.title: Trans fats (depending on oil)
items.content: If partially hydrogenated oil is used for frying, trans fats may be present, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Corn chips can be enjoyed straight from the bag, added to salads, used as a base for nachos with cheese, guacamole or salsa, and incorporated into Mexican dishes such as tacos and chili.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep chips in a sealed container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store them in the refrigerator to prevent oil oxidation.
